The forwarders complain that this situation leaves them at the motor carriers' mercy and makes it impossible for the forwarder to exercise proper control over its freight movements. An added problem has been short-haul motor carrier cancellation of or refusal to enter into Section 409 contracts. Section 409 allows motor carriers to provide pickup and delivery services beyond terminal area limits and freight forwarders to enter into contracts with them for such services.
The forwarders assert that expanded terminal areas will result in substantial service improvement, especially on small shipments, and will enable forwarders to control directly and supervise pickup and delivery throughout urban areas. This would result in faster, more reliable service, less handling and less freight damage. Furthermore, it is argued that the added competition from forwarders would force motor carriers to give better service. The forwarders state that the establishment of more terminal facilities will not solve their operational problems, because they already have as many terminals as present traffic flow will permit.
The Freight Forwarder Institute supported its request for expansion of terminal areas by a report prepared by a research and consulting firm entitled "An Assessment of the Population-Mileage Formula."
